points.description: States that a binary search tree is a binary tree (each node has at most two children, a left child and a right child). Equivalent wording earns the mark.

States the ordering property that holds for any node: the left child is smaller than the parent, and the parent is smaller than the right child. Equivalent wording earns the mark, for example stating that the left subtree holds smaller values and the right subtree holds larger values. The property must be stated for every node, not just the root.

deductions.description: Gives the ordering in the wrong direction, such as left child larger than the parent or right child smaller than the parent.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both that it is a binary tree and that every node satisfies left < parent < right (or an equivalent statement of the ordering). A student who describes only the binary structure, or only a partial or root-only ordering, earns the structural mark or part of the ordering mark, but not full credit. Equivalent wording, such as a subtree-based description of the ordering, is accepted.
